rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 (mass 0.6, all else as iteration 7) is the best raced design at 700.01, up from 687.06. Its oval finished 20/20 (max_error 0.008, steering_oscillation 0.21) and its s-bend finished 20/20 (steering_oscillation 0.31, progress 0.998). The slalom is still the binding track: 0/20 finishes, progress 0.52 (up from 0.45), max_error 0.065, 1.35 line-loss events, all ending off track. The mass change moved the slalom the most of any lever tested since iteration 3.

What the record rules out: kp 4.0 (slalom progress down), kd 0.7 vs 0.8 (kd helps the s-bend but cuts slalom progress), base_speed 1.2 (cost on oval and s-bend), sensor y 0.06 vs 0.08 (0.08 helped), 16 mm footprints (neutral), lateral widening to 0.045 m (slalom progress down) and narrowing to 0.02 m (slalom progress down, 676.7). The geometry and gain levers are exhausted at the current settings.

Decision: submit the iteration 10 design unchanged, mass 0.6. The Evaluator approved this exact build, and it is the best measured result (700.01) with all three development tracks finishing or nearly so on oval and s-bend. I considered the Evaluator's suggested next test (mass 0.5), but this is the final iteration: no later race can revert it, and an unapproved build scores 0. The untested 0.5 value carries an unmeasured risk to the oval and s-bend, so it is not worth that exposure now.

Expected result: about 700 on the development tracks, with the same profile as iteration 10. The unseen track is the main uncertainty. Measurements requested: all metrics, so the final race can be compared per track against iteration 10.
